admitted_candidate.claim_boundary: Static sidecar artifact. No hardware measurement. No weight write. Abliteration is a candidate transformation generator; it does not guarantee removal of refusals (NousResearch/llm-abliteration README). A result may name a candidate direction, a stated projection, and the completion / harmless / loss evaluations that selected it. It may not report a model as abliterated, uncensored, or refusal-free.

after.unit: selected candidate transformations / hour (not direction-candidates / hour)

before.unit: selected candidate transformations / hour (not direction-candidates / hour)

bench.rule: wall times are wall_s measured with perf_counter; no tps/wall_ns/gpu_ns field is written

claim_boundary: Abliteration is a candidate transformation generator, not an uncensoring switch. This receipt records a real run on a whole-tree-verified specimen: direction candidates from real activations, multi-objective selection, an in-memory weight-space projection, per-step wall times, and a repatriation map. It does not write ModelLake. It does not claim the child is abliterated, uncensored, or refusal-free. A behavioural outcome that was not generation-evaluated is UNMEASURED. Upstream (NousResearch/llm-abliteration README) does not guarantee complete removal of refusals.

confirmation.note: in-memory child; lake not written; KL is not a behavioural eval

failspy.sort: single score = completion (harmful residual alignment); NOT harmless+loss gates

filter_train.rule: empty after filter is a refusal-direction run refusal; this generator still emits a contrast direction on the declared sets, labelled as such

generation_eval.reason: no completion strings were sampled; hooked/activation scores are not a behavioural measurement

reasons: FailSpy: blacklist first and last couple destination layers by default
andyrdt: prune last 0.2 of layers as direction SOURCES (cutoff=22)

negative_findings: upstream does not guarantee complete removal of refusals; this module will not manufacture that guarantee
FailSpy's find_best_refusal_dir is a single-score sort and is treated as a negative control, not a method
a directory named 'abliterated' is a naming fact, not a verified behavioural outcome
ModelLake was not written; the child exists in memory and as this receipt

outer_scorer.reason: no generation-level ScoreVector was measured; independent vector stays UNMEASURED

kind.why: smallest recovered residual-stream causal LM on this lake

port_rule: the obligation asked what repatriates; an honest map is the deliverable
purpose: Run abliteration as a first-class Tabula candidate-transformation generator on a whole-tree-verified specimen, measure what it generated, map which steps repatriate to Rust/Metal, and cut the wall so the generator yields more results per unit time.

repatriation.reason: fcntl flock of a lockfile is process coordination, not tensor work
JSON row lookup; already a Python sidecar
byte copy USB→SSD; os/cp, not a Metal kernel. Staging is the I/O cut, not a port
safetensors → device. hawking-core already loads Qwen weights onto Metal; transformers+MPS is a stand-in, not the resident loader
this repo already tokenizes Qwen in Rust; the Python tokenizer is not the bottleneck
first-forward shader/pipeline setup on MPS. A resident Metal runtime that already compiled the Qwen graph would not pay this again
same forwards, sequential instead of batched; the batch is the Python-side cut, the kernel is still a Metal prefill
batched prefill over residual-stream layers. hawking-core Metal decode/prefill already runs Qwen forwards; this is the wall that repatriates
mean-subtract + normalize per layer. Pure tensor, d_model=1024, microseconds on CPU; Metal would not move the end-to-end wall
projections, energy fractions, optional hooked prefills and last-token KL. The hooked prefills are the same Metal forwards; the matvecs are lm_head, which hawking-core already issues
a sort of N≈28 scalars; not tensor work
tools.future.abliteration.select control flow; not tensor work
W'=(I-vv^T)W plus row-norm restore on o_proj and down_proj. Rank-1 update / GEMM. hawking-core already has Metal matmul and o_proj gemv (crates/hawking-core/src/metal, shaders/matmul.metal)
one batched prefill on the in-memory projected child; same Metal forward as capture

selection.claim: candidate direction selected under completion+harmless+loss gates; this is not an uncensoring result
selection.tie_break: source_layer, source_position, id — NOT a quality ranking

selector_comparison.why_it_matters: FailSpy's single-score sort is the refusal-suppression-only choice the method makes inexpressible. Disagreement is a result, not a bug.

speed.connects_to: IMPROVEMENT_VELOCITY — a generator nobody can afford to run generates nothing
cuts_applied: SSD stage of the 1.5 GiB specimen off USB ModelLake (I/O cut)
one padded batched prefill for activation capture instead of per-prompt sequential forwards
last-token only (not Arditi's full position grid)
no generation-eval loop per candidate (behaviour UNMEASURED rather than 28×N generate)
hooked last-token eval sampled (2 candidates) + selected child, not 28×2 prefills
MPS biprojection of dest o_proj/down_proj; numpy geometry on one sample matrix
speed.what_cutting_the_rest_requires: Keeping the model resident across generator calls (amortize model_load / mps_first_forward / verification). A native hawking-core Qwen prefill that is already warm would remove mps_first_forward. Porting the rank-1 biprojection to an existing Metal matmul would cut weight_projection further only after load is amortized.
